title: Efficacy of Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Mpox Virus Infection in Humans: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Tecovirimat has been widely used for the treatment of mpox despite limited evidence supporting its efficacy. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tecovirimat for this purpose. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to June 5, 2026 for RCTs comparing tecovirimat with placebo or standard care in patients with laboratory-confirmed mpox. Primary outcomes were time to clinical resolution of skin lesions, clinical resolution by day 28-29, and 28-day all-cause mortality. Hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Two low-risk-of-bias RCTs involving 941 participants were included. Tecovirimat did not shorten the time to clinical resolution of skin lesions compared with placebo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.52-2.31, GRADE: moderate) or increase the lesion resolution by day 28-29 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.92-1.08, GRADE: high). No statistical heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 0% for both outcomes). Mortality at day 28 was rare in both trials, precluding meta-analysis. Virological clearance, pain-related outcomes, and serious adverse events were also comparable between treatment groups. In conclusion, current randomized evidence does not support routine tecovirimat use to accelerate clinical recovery or improve mortality rates in patients with mpox, while further evidence is needed to determine whether selected high-risk populations may benefit from antiviral therapy.

title: Community knowledge and perceptions of social, ecological, and behavioural risk factors for mpox in Burundi: A nationwide cross-sectional survey
abstract: Mpox remains an important public health concern in Africa, particularly following the spread of clade Ib in several countries. In Burundi, limited information is available on population knowledge, risk perception, preventive behaviours, and willingness to accept mpox vaccination. This study assessed social and behavioural factors associated with mpox preparedness among the general population. We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey between March and December 2025 across five provinces of Burundi. A total of 5,177 participants aged 15 years and older were interviewed using a structured questionnaire adapted from the Africa CDC behavioural and social sciences framework for mpox. Sampling weights were not applied; therefore, findings should be interpreted as estimates among surveyed participants rather than nationally weighted population estimates. Univariate analyses were conducted to describe key variables, while bivariate and multivariable analyses using modified Poisson regression models with generalized estimating equations were performed to identify factors associated with mpox knowledge and prevention and control practices. Overall, most participants had heard about mpox (94.7%). Many correctly identified skin rash (94.4%) and fever (84.3%) as common symptoms, and most recognized direct contact as a mode of transmission (86.6%). However, 21.4% of participants incorrectly identified bacteria as the causative agent and 24.5% did not know the causative agent. Radio was the main source of information (82.0%) and the most trusted source (87.0%). Higher income was associated with better mpox knowledge. Prevention and control practices varied by knowledge level, income, marital status, and HIV status. Although most participants (86.1%) were unaware of the availability of a vaccine, 76.5% reported willingness to accept vaccination if available. Despite high awareness and willingness to accept vaccination, important gaps in mpox knowledge remain, particularly among lower-income groups. Strengthening accessible and targeted risk communication strategies will be essential to improve mpox preparedness in Burundi.

title_zh: 布隆迪 猴痘 的社区知识和对社会、生态和行为风险因素的看法:全国横断面调查
source_body_en: Mpox remains an important public health concern in Africa, particularly following the spread of clade Ib in several countries. In Burundi, limited information is available on population knowledge, risk perception, preventive behaviours, and willingness to accept mpox vaccination. This study assessed social and behavioural factors associated with mpox preparedness among the general population. We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey between March and December 2025 across five provinces of Burundi. A total of 5,177 participants aged 15 years and older were interviewed using a structured questionnaire adapted from the Africa CDC behavioural and social sciences framework for mpox. Sampling weights were not applied; therefore, findings should be interpreted as estimates among surveyed participants rather than nationally weighted population estimates. Univariate analyses were conducted to describe key variables, while bivariate and multivariable analyses using modified Poisson regression models with generalized estimating equations were performed to identify factors associated with mpox knowledge and prevention and control practices. Overall, most participants had heard about mpox (94.7%). Many correctly identified skin rash (94.4%) and fever (84.3%) as common symptoms, and most recognized direct contact as a mode of transmission (86.6%). However, 21.4% of participants incorrectly identified bacteria as the causative agent and 24.5% did not know the causative agent. Radio was the main source of information (82.0%) and the most trusted source (87.0%). Higher income was associated with better mpox knowledge. Prevention and control practices varied by knowledge level, income, marital status, and HIV status. Although most participants (86.1%) were unaware of the availability of a vaccine, 76.5% reported willingness to accept vaccination if available. Despite high awareness and willingness to accept vaccination, important gaps in mpox knowledge remain, particularly among lower-income groups. Strengthening accessible and targeted risk communication strategies will be essential to improve mpox preparedness in Burundi.
abstract_zh: 猴痘 仍然是非洲的一个重要公共卫生问题,特别是在 Ib 分支在几个国家传播之后。在布隆迪,关于人口知识、风险认知、预防行为和接受 猴痘 疫苗接种 的意愿的信息有限。本研究评估了普通人群中与 猴痘 准备情况相关的社会和行为因素。我们于 2025 年 3 月至 12 月期间在布隆迪的五个省份进行了全国横断面调查。使用改编自非洲疾病预防控制中心 猴痘 行为和社会科学框架的结构化调查问卷,对总共 5,177 名 15 岁及以上的参与者进行了采访。未应用抽样权重;因此,调查结果应解释为受调查参与者的估计,而不是全国加权的人口估计。进行单变量分析来描述关键变量,同时使用带有广义估计方程的修正泊松回归模型进行双变量和多变量分析,以确定与猴痘知识和预防和控制实践相关的因素。总体而言,大多数参与者听说过 猴痘(94.7%)。许多人正确地将皮疹(94.4%)和发烧(84.3%)视为常见症状,并且大多数人认为直接接触是 传播 的一种模式(86.6%)。然而,21.4% 的参与者错误地将细菌识别为病原体,24.5% 的参与者不知道病原体。广播是主要的信息来源(82.0%),也是最值得信赖的来源(87.0%)。更高的收入与更好的 猴痘 知识相关。预防和控制做法因知识水平、收入、婚姻状况和艾滋病毒状况而异。尽管大多数参与者 (86.1%) 不知道 疫苗 的可用性,但 76.5% 的参与者表示愿意接受 疫苗接种(如果有)。尽管接受 疫苗接种 的意识和意愿很高,但 猴痘 知识仍然存在重大差距,特别是在低收入群体中。加强可及且有针对性的风险沟通策略对于改善布隆迪的 猴痘 准备工作至关重要。

title: Peer Review Report For: Case Report: Conducting Clinical Trials during an Outbreak: An Mpox case report [version 2; peer review: 1 approved, 1 approved with reservations]
abstract: Background: Conducting clinical trials during infectious disease outbreaks presents operational, ethical, and methodological challenges. During the 2024–2025 Mpox outbreak in Uganda, an Mpox case occurred within an HIV-focused clinical trial requiring immediate operational and ethical response. The trial aimed to assess the feasibility of therapeutic drug monitoring and optimize antimicrobial therapy in people living with HIV. Case presentation We report the case of an adult man living with HIV enrolled in the Therapeutic Drug Monitoring for Antimicrobial Agents for People Living with HIV (TAP) trial at a tertiary HIV clinic in Uganda. Following initiation of antimicrobial therapy and study enrolment, at a scheduled study follow-up visit, he developed a vesiculopustular rash involving the face and upper limbs. Research staff promptly activated infection prevention and control measures, halted study procedures, and notified the national surveillance team. Mpox infection was confirmed by real-time polymerase chain reaction testing. The participant was transferred to a designated isolation facility for clinical management and withdrawn from the trial. Continuity of HIV care was maintained through remote (phone) adherence counselling and coordination of antiretroviral refills. No secondary cases were identified among study participants or personnel after 21 days of self-monitoring. Conclusions This report highlights the importance of outbreak preparedness, adaptive risk management, and rapid coordination with public health teams to safeguard participants and personnel, protect research integrity, and ensure continuity of essential clinical care during epidemics.

abstract_zh: 背景:在传染病 暴发 期间进行临床试验提出了操作、伦理和方法学方面的挑战。2024-2025 年乌干达 猴痘 暴发 期间,在一项以 HIV 为重点的临床试验中发生了一起 猴痘 病例,需要立即采取操作和伦理反应。该试验旨在评估治疗药物监测的可行性并优化艾滋病毒感染者的抗菌治疗。病例介绍 我们报告了一名成年男性艾滋病毒感染者的病例,该男子参加了乌干达一家三级艾滋病毒诊所的艾滋病毒感染者抗菌药物治疗药物监测 (TAP) 试验。在开始抗菌治疗和研究入组后,在预定的研究随访中,他出现了涉及面部和上肢的水疱脓疱性皮疹。研究人员迅速启动感染防控措施,暂停研究程序,并通知国家监测团队。通过实时聚合酶链反应检测证实了猴痘感染。参与者被转移到指定的隔离设施进行临床管理并退出试验。通过远程(电话)依从性咨询和抗逆转录病毒药物补充协调来维持艾滋病毒护理的连续性。经过 21 天的自我监测后,研究参与者或人员中没有发现继发病例。结论 本报告强调了 暴发 准备、适应性风险管理以及与公共卫生团队快速协调的重要性,以保护参与者和人员、保护研究完整性并确保流行病期间基本临床护理的连续性。

title: Epidemiological trajectory of Mpox in Brazil, 2022-2025: evidence of geographic consolidation and syndemic burden.
abstract: Mpox has transitioned from outbreak to sustained transmission in Brazil, a country with high ecological and social connectivity. We analysed the epidemiological trajectory of mpox during 2022-2025 using 14 475 laboratory-confirmed cases reported by the Brazilian Ministry of Health. Our findings indicate geographical consolidation of transmission, with the highest incidence observed in the southeast and midwest regions. The epidemic disproportionately affects men (93.0%), particularly young adults, with transmission primarily associated with networks of men who have sex with men (69.1%). A substantial burden of co-infections was identified: 47.1% of reported cases occurred in persons living with HIV and 30.8% had syphilis. Clinically, most patients presented with cutaneous manifestations (91.3%). These findings highlight the convergence of epidemiological and social determinants shaping mpox transmission in Brazil. Strengthening integrated surveillance systems and ensuring equitable, stigma-free access to prevention and care are critical to reducing transmission and mitigating the risk of broader dissemination.

title: КОНТРОЛЬ КАЧЕСТВА И СТАБИЛЬНОСТЬ ВАКЦИН ПРОТИВ MPOX: СОВРЕМЕННЫЕ КРИТЕРИИ И ПОДХОДЫ QUALITY CONTROL AND STABILITY OF MPOX VACCINES: MODERN CRITERIA AND APPROACHES
abstract: This article presents a comparative analysis of current requirements for stability assessment and quality control of mpox vaccines in accordance with the recommendations of the World Health Organization (WHO), the regulatory framework of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH), and the Republic of Kazakhstan. The main approaches to stability testing of immunobiological products are discussed, including long-term and accelerated studies, their objectives, testing conditions, and their role in establishing vaccine shelf life. The review systematizes the principal quality attributes used in vaccine stability assessment, including physicochemical parameters (appearance, pH, and homogeneity), biological characteristics (infectious titer, antigen content, immunogenicity, and genetic stability), safety indicators (toxicity, pyrogenicity, and reversion to virulence), and microbiological purity. It is shown that deviations from recommended storage temperatures, as well as exposure to light and moisture and disruptions in the cold chain, may lead to degradation of antigenic components and a decline in vaccine immunogenicity. Additional attention is given to the characteristics of currently available mpox vaccines, including ACAM2000, JYNNEOS, LC16m8, and OrthopoxVac, with emphasis on vaccine platform, replicative properties, and storage conditions. The analysis demonstrated that international and regional regulatory requirements are generally harmonized; however, certain differences remain in approaches to stability studies and quality control procedures. The findings highlight the need for further improvement of the national regulatory framework and the implementation of advanced methods for assessing vaccine biological activity.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the quality control and stability of mpox vaccines, examining the criteria and approaches recommended by international and regional regulatory bodies such as the World Health Organization (WHO), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH), and the Republic of Kazakhstan. The central question is how these requirements influence vaccine stability and quality assurance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of current standards and practices for vaccine stability testing and quality control. It discusses the main approaches to stability testing, including long-term and accelerated studies, their objectives, testing conditions, and their role in determining vaccine shelf life. The evidence is based on the recommendations of regulatory bodies and the characteristics of available mpox vaccines.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that international and regional regulatory requirements for mpox vaccine stability and quality control are generally harmonized, although differences exist in approaches to stability studies and procedures. It also highlights the importance of physicochemical, biological, safety, and microbiological parameters in vaccine stability assessment.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that deviations from recommended storage conditions, such as exposure to light, moisture, or temperature fluctuations, may lead to antigen degradation and reduced immunogenicity. However, it does not provide a detailed analysis of the specific mechanisms or the extent of these effects. Additionally, the review emphasizes the need for further improvements in national regulatory frameworks and the implementation of advanced methods for assessing vaccine biological activity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for enhanced national regulatory frameworks and the adoption of advanced methods for evaluating vaccine biological activity. This includes improving storage conditions and monitoring the stability of vaccines under various environmental factors to ensure their efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This review article provides a comprehensive analysis of the quality control and stability criteria for mpox vaccines, emphasizing the alignment of international and regional standards. It outlines the main approaches to stability testing, including long-term and accelerated studies, and highlights the key parameters used in vaccine assessment. The review identifies potential issues with vaccine degradation due to improper storage conditions and calls for improvements in regulatory frameworks and testing methods to enhance vaccine safety and effectiveness.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the quality control and stability of mpox vaccines, examining the criteria and approaches recommended by international and regional regulatory bodies such as the World Health Organization (WHO), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH), and the Republic of Kazakhstan. The central question is how these requirements influence vaccine stability and quality assurance.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of current standards and practices for vaccine stability testing and quality control. It discusses the main approaches to stability testing, including long-term and accelerated studies, their objectives, testing conditions, and their role in determining vaccine shelf life. The evidence is based on the recommendations of regulatory bodies and the characteristics of available mpox vaccines.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that international and regional regulatory requirements for mpox vaccine stability and quality control are generally harmonized, although differences exist in approaches to stability studies and procedures. It also highlights the importance of physicochemical, biological, safety, and microbiological parameters in vaccine stability assessment.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that deviations from recommended storage conditions, such as exposure to light, moisture, or temperature fluctuations, may lead to antigen degradation and reduced immunogenicity. However, it does not provide a detailed analysis of the specific mechanisms or the extent of these effects. Additionally, the review emphasizes the need for further improvements in national regulatory frameworks and the implementation of advanced methods for assessing vaccine biological activity.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for enhanced national regulatory frameworks and the adoption of advanced methods for evaluating vaccine biological activity. title_zh: КОНТРОЛЬ КАЧЕСТВА И СТАБИЛЬНОСТЬ ВАКЦИН ПРОТИВ 猴痘: СОВРЕМЕННЫЕ КИТЕРИИ И 猴痘 疫苗 的质量控制和稳定性:现代标准和方法
source_body_en: This article presents a comparative analysis of current requirements for stability assessment and quality control of mpox vaccines in accordance with the recommendations of the World Health Organization (WHO), the regulatory framework of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH), and the Republic of Kazakhstan. The main approaches to stability testing of immunobiological products are discussed, including long-term and accelerated studies, their objectives, testing conditions, and their role in establishing vaccine shelf life. The review systematizes the principal quality attributes used in vaccine stability assessment, including physicochemical parameters (appearance, pH, and homogeneity), biological characteristics (infectious titer, antigen content, immunogenicity, and genetic stability), safety indicators (toxicity, pyrogenicity, and reversion to virulence), and microbiological purity. It is shown that deviations from recommended storage temperatures, as well as exposure to light and moisture and disruptions in the cold chain, may lead to degradation of antigenic components and a decline in vaccine immunogenicity. Additional attention is given to the characteristics of currently available mpox vaccines, including ACAM2000, JYNNEOS, LC16m8, and OrthopoxVac, with emphasis on vaccine platform, replicative properties, and storage conditions. The analysis demonstrated that international and regional regulatory requirements are generally harmonized; however, certain differences remain in approaches to stability studies and quality control procedures. The findings highlight the need for further improvement of the national regulatory framework and the implementation of advanced methods for assessing vaccine biological activity.

title: Isoform-Resolved Temporal Remodeling of Transcriptome Architecture in Monkeypox Virus
abstract: Abstract We reanalyzed previously generated replicated Oxford Nanopore direct cDNA sequencing data from six infection time points, together with cap analysis of gene expression and native direct RNA sequencing, to reconstruct full-length monkeypox virus transcripts and characterize their temporal regulation. A broad catalogue of candidate transcript models, including candidate 5′ poly(A)-associated structures, was filtered with independent 5′- and 3′-end evidence to define conservative analysis sets. Transcript-resolved profiles revealed a structured temporal program extending beyond gene-level abundance. Host-virus interaction, transcription, and nucleotide-metabolism genes contributed strongly early, whereas virion structure and morphogenesis genes dominated later. Transcription start and end site abundance profiles changed extensively over time, and many genes redistributed among alternative full-length transcript structures. Differential transcript usage was particularly prominent among host-virus interaction genes but depleted among virion structure and morphogenesis genes. Candidate 5′ poly(A)-associated transcripts also increased in relative contribution and showed locus-specific patterns. Building on our previous endpoint map, the replicated direct cDNA time course enabled temporal quantification of gene abundance, transcript-end dynamics, and isoform composition. Together, these results show that Monkeypox virus gene regulation involves coordinated remodeling of gene output, transcript boundaries, and full-length transcriptome architecture. Importance Monkeypox virus is an emerging human pathogen with the capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission, making a detailed understanding of its molecular biology increasingly important. Viral replication depends on coordinated gene expression, and defining when and how viral genes are transcribed is essential for understanding infection. Complete transcript structures provide information that gene-level measurements cannot capture because alternative RNA forms can differ in regulatory regions, coding potential, and capacity for translation. Resolving the organization and temporal use of these transcripts therefore helps reveal how the virus controls protein production and interacts with the host cell. A transcript-level view of monkeypox virus gene regulation provides a foundation for mechanistic studies of poxvirus biology and may help identify regulatory processes or viral functions relevant to antiviral intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the temporal remodeling of the monkeypox virus transcriptome, focusing on how gene expression and transcript structures change during infection. By reanalyzing Oxford Nanopore direct cDNA sequencing data from six time points, along with cap analysis of gene expression and native direct RNA sequencing, the researchers reconstructed full-length transcripts and characterized their regulation. The results show a structured temporal program, with early emphasis on host-virus interaction and transcription genes, and later dominance of virion structure and morphogenesis genes. Additionally, candidate 5′ poly(A)-associated transcripts increased in relative contribution and displayed locus-specific patterns. These findings highlight the coordinated changes in gene output, transcript boundaries, and full-length transcriptome architecture, offering insights into viral regulation and potential targets for antiviral strategies. The study's reliance on existing data limits its novelty, but the integration of multiple sequencing approaches provides a moderate level of confidence in the results.

title_zh: 猴痘病毒转录组结构的异构体解析时间重塑
source_body_en: Abstract We reanalyzed previously generated replicated Oxford Nanopore direct cDNA sequencing data from six infection time points, together with cap analysis of gene expression and native direct RNA sequencing, to reconstruct full-length monkeypox virus transcripts and characterize their temporal regulation. A broad catalogue of candidate transcript models, including candidate 5′ poly(A)-associated structures, was filtered with independent 5′- and 3′-end evidence to define conservative analysis sets. Transcript-resolved profiles revealed a structured temporal program extending beyond gene-level abundance. Host-virus interaction, transcription, and nucleotide-metabolism genes contributed strongly early, whereas virion structure and morphogenesis genes dominated later. Transcription start and end site abundance profiles changed extensively over time, and many genes redistributed among alternative full-length transcript structures. Differential transcript usage was particularly prominent among host-virus interaction genes but depleted among virion structure and morphogenesis genes. Candidate 5′ poly(A)-associated transcripts also increased in relative contribution and showed locus-specific patterns. Building on our previous endpoint map, the replicated direct cDNA time course enabled temporal quantification of gene abundance, transcript-end dynamics, and isoform composition. Together, these results show that Monkeypox virus gene regulation involves coordinated remodeling of gene output, transcript boundaries, and full-length transcriptome architecture. Importance Monkeypox virus is an emerging human pathogen with the capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission, making a detailed understanding of its molecular biology increasingly important. Viral replication depends on coordinated gene expression, and defining when and how viral genes are transcribed is essential for understanding infection. Complete transcript structures provide information that gene-level measurements cannot capture because alternative RNA forms can differ in regulatory regions, coding potential, and capacity for translation. Resolving the organization and temporal use of these transcripts therefore helps reveal how the virus controls protein production and interacts with the host cell. A transcript-level view of monkeypox virus gene regulation provides a foundation for mechanistic studies of poxvirus biology and may help identify regulatory processes or viral functions relevant to antiviral intervention.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding priority zoonotic diseases (Mpox, Ebola, and Rabies) and associated factors among households in Bukavu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2025
abstract: Abstract Background: Zoonotic diseases are a major public health concern in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where diseases such as rabies, Ebola, and Mpox pose ongoing health risks. Household knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) play an important role in preventing zoonotic disease transmission. This study assessed household knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding priority zoonotic diseases in Bukavu, South Kivu Province, DRC, and identified factors associated with satisfactory overall KAP. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from September 1 to 15, 2025, in the Bagira and Kadutu health zones of Bukavu. A total of 634 households were selected using two-stage cluster sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered through KoboCollect and analyzed using Stata version 17. The questionnaire assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices concerning Ebola, Mpox, and rabies. Knowledge was measured using 17 items, attitudes using five-point Likert-scale items, and practices using five behavioral items. Scores of at least 70% were classified as satisfactory. Descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used. Nonparametric tests were used when appropriate. Associations were reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Overall, 42.9% of households demonstrated satisfactory knowledge of zoonotic diseases, 63.6% had favorable attitudes, and 11.7% demonstrated adequate preventive practices. Mpox was recognized as a zoonosis by 78.2% of respondents, Ebola by 66.6%, and rabies by 39.1%. Knowledge scores were higher among livestock-farming than non-livestock-farming households (p = 0.002). In the multivariable analysis of overall KAP, university-level education (OR = 12.06; 95% CI: 1.54-94.18; p = 0.018) and access to drinking water (OR = 6.74; 95% CI: 3.91-11.60; p < 0.001) were positively associated with satisfactory overall KAP. Conclusions: Households in Bukavu reported generally favorable attitudes toward zoonotic disease prevention, but satisfactory knowledge was less widespread and adequate preventive practices were uncommon. Interventions should help translate awareness and favorable attitudes into practical preventive behaviors through targeted risk communication and health education, alongside improvements in access to drinking water and sanitation. A coordinated One Health approach involving human, animal, and environmental health stakeholders may strengthen household-level prevention of priority zoonotic diseases. The findings can help inform locally tailored prevention strategies and identify priorities for future community-based research. Keywords: Zoonoses; Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices; One Health; Bukavu; Democratic Republic of the Congo

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估刚果民主共和国布卡武家庭对重点人畜共患疾病(包括 猴痘、埃博拉病毒和狂犬病)的知识、态度和做法 (KAP),以确定与总体 KAP 令人满意相关的因素。人畜共患疾病是刚果民主共和国的一个主要公共卫生问题,狂犬病、埃博拉病毒和 猴痘 等疾病持续构成健康风险。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年 9 月 1 日至 15 日在刚果民主共和国南基伍省布卡武的巴吉拉和卡杜图卫生区进行了一项横断面研究。采用两阶段整群抽样方法,共抽取了 634 户家庭。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 KoboCollect 管理的结构化调查问卷收集数据,并使用 Stata 版本 17 进行分析。调查问卷评估了有关埃博拉病毒、猴痘 和狂犬病的知识、态度和做法。知识使用 17 个项目进行测量,态度使用五点李克特量表项目进行测量,实践使用五个行为项目进行测量。至少 70% 的分数被列为满意。使用描述性统计、组间比较以及双变量和多变量逻辑回归分析。在适当的时候使用非参数检验。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,42.9%的家庭对人畜共患疾病的了解令人满意,63.6%的家庭持积极态度,11.7%的家庭表现出足够的预防措施。78.2% 的受访者将 猴痘 视为 人兽共患病,埃博拉为 66.6%,狂犬病为 39.1%。畜牧业家庭的知识得分高于非畜牧业家庭(p = 0.002)。在总体 KAP 的多变量分析中,大学教育(OR = 12.06;95% CI:1.54-94.18;p = 0.018)和饮用水获取情况(OR = 6.74;95% CI:3.91-11.60;p < 0.001)与令人满意的总体 KAP 呈正相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,布卡武的家庭普遍对人畜共患疾病预防持积极态度,但令人满意的知识普及程度较低,适当的预防措施也不常见。该研究确定了与总体 KAP 满意度呈正相关的具体因素,例如大学教育和饮用水的获取。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以帮助为当地制定预防策略提供信息,并确定未来基于社区的研究的优先事项。干预措施应通过有针对性的风险沟通和健康教育,以及改善饮用水和卫生设施的获取,帮助将认识和积极态度转化为实际的预防行为。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横断面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系,并且可能存在自我报告偏差。由于该研究的观察性质和缺乏纵向数据,证据强度中等。

title_zh: 2025 年刚果民主共和国布卡武家庭对重点人畜共患疾病(猴痘、埃博拉和狂犬病)的知识、态度和做法以及相关因素
source_body_en: Abstract Background: Zoonotic diseases are a major public health concern in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where diseases such as rabies, Ebola, and Mpox pose ongoing health risks. Household knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) play an important role in preventing zoonotic disease transmission. This study assessed household knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding priority zoonotic diseases in Bukavu, South Kivu Province, DRC, and identified factors associated with satisfactory overall KAP. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from September 1 to 15, 2025, in the Bagira and Kadutu health zones of Bukavu. A total of 634 households were selected using two-stage cluster sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered through KoboCollect and analyzed using Stata version 17. The questionnaire assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices concerning Ebola, Mpox, and rabies. Knowledge was measured using 17 items, attitudes using five-point Likert-scale items, and practices using five behavioral items. Scores of at least 70% were classified as satisfactory. Descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used. Nonparametric tests were used when appropriate. Associations were reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Overall, 42.9% of households demonstrated satisfactory knowledge of zoonotic diseases, 63.6% had favorable attitudes, and 11.7% demonstrated adequate preventive practices. Mpox was recognized as a zoonosis by 78.2% of respondents, Ebola by 66.6%, and rabies by 39.1%. Knowledge scores were higher among livestock-farming than non-livestock-farming households (p = 0.002). In the multivariable analysis of overall KAP, university-level education (OR = 12.06; 95% CI: 1.54-94.18; p = 0.018) and access to drinking water (OR = 6.74; 95% CI: 3.91-11.60; p < 0.001) were positively associated with satisfactory overall KAP. Conclusions: Households in Bukavu reported generally favorable attitudes toward zoonotic disease prevention, but satisfactory knowledge was less widespread and adequate preventive practices were uncommon. Interventions should help translate awareness and favorable attitudes into practical preventive behaviors through targeted risk communication and health education, alongside improvements in access to drinking water and sanitation. A coordinated One Health approach involving human, animal, and environmental health stakeholders may strengthen household-level prevention of priority zoonotic diseases. The findings can help inform locally tailored prevention strategies and identify priorities for future community-based research. Keywords: Zoonoses; Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices; One Health; Bukavu; Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract_zh: 摘要背景:人畜共患疾病是刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 的主要公共卫生问题,狂犬病、埃博拉病毒和 猴痘 等疾病对该国构成持续的健康风险。家庭知识、态度和实践(KAP)在预防人畜共患疾病方面发挥着重要作用 传播。本研究评估了刚果民主共和国南基伍省布卡武的家庭对重点人畜共患疾病的知识、态度和做法,并确定了与总体 KAP 满意度相关的因素。方法:2025 年 9 月 1 日至 15 日在布卡武的巴吉拉和卡杜图卫生区进行了一项横断面研究。采用两阶段整群抽样方法,共抽取了 634 户家庭。使用 KoboCollect 管理的结构化调查问卷收集数据,并使用 Stata 版本 17 进行分析。调查问卷评估了有关埃博拉病毒、猴痘 和狂犬病的知识、态度和做法。知识使用 17 个项目进行测量,态度使用五点李克特量表项目进行测量,实践使用五个行为项目进行测量。至少 70% 的分数被列为满意。使用描述性统计、组间比较以及双变量和多变量逻辑回归分析。在适当的时候使用非参数检验。相关性以比值比 (OR) 和 95% 置信区间 (CI) 报告,p < 0.05 被认为具有统计显着性。结果:总体而言,42.9%的家庭对人畜共患疾病的了解令人满意,63.6%的家庭持良好态度,11.7%的家庭表现出足够的预防措施。78.2% 的受访者将 猴痘 视为 人兽共患病,埃博拉为 66.6%,狂犬病为 39.1%。畜牧业家庭的知识得分高于非畜牧业家庭(p = 0.002)。在总体 KAP 的多变量分析中,大学教育(OR = 12.06;95% CI:1.54-94.18;p = 0.018)和饮用水获取情况(OR = 6.74;95% CI:3.91-11.60;p < 0.001)与令人满意的总体 KAP 呈正相关。结论:布卡武家庭对人畜共患疾病预防普遍持积极态度,但令人满意的知识普及程度较低,适当的预防措施也不常见。干预措施应通过有针对性的风险沟通和健康教育,以及改善饮用水和卫生设施的获取,帮助将认识和积极态度转化为实际的预防行为。涉及人类、动物和环境健康利益相关者的协调一致的“同一个健康”方法可以加强家庭层面对重点人畜共患疾病的预防。研究结果可以帮助为当地制定预防策略提供信息,并确定未来基于社区的研究的优先事项。关键词:人畜共患病;知识、态度和实践;一个健康;布卡武;刚果民主共和国

title: Hybrid architectures of CNN-ViT and SE-CNN with grad-CAM for monkeypox disease detection
abstract: Abstract In the aftermath of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the monkeypox virus (MPV) emerged as a significant global health concern, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare it a public health emergency. Accurate detection of monkeypox (Mpox) is challenging due to its similarity to other pox viruses such as measles and chickenpox. Conventional diagnostic methods often struggle to distinguish between these diseases, necessitating the development of more advanced diagnostic tools. This paper presents a novel approach to detect Mpox using two efficient deep learning (DL) models: the first one is a hybrid architecture of a Convolutional Neural Network—Vision Transformer (CNN–ViT), and the second model is a Squeeze-and-Excitation Convolutional Neural Network (SE-CNN). These models are employed for the classification of medical images into two categories: Monkeypox and Others. The proposed models are applied to a dataset of 1140 images, and utilize fine-tuning for the models’ hyperparameters. Data augmentation techniques are implemented for training images to maximize the models’ performance. Additionally, a gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization technique is applied to explain the decision of the models and aid doctors in clinical decision-making. Experimentally, the accuracy, error matrix, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, Recall, F1-score, and Precision are used to measure the performance of the proposed models. The CNN–ViT and SE-CNN achieve a testing accuracy of 97.80% and 96.05%, respectively, while the micro-average area under the ROC curve is 97% for CNN–ViT and 99% for SE-CNN. The weighted F1-score, Precision, and Recall for CNN–ViT are all 97.26%, 97.33%, and 97.27%, respectively, while for SE-CNN are 96.04%, 96.13%, and 96.05%, respectively. The proposed models provide a rapid and accurate method to differentiate Mpox from other cases, offering a valuable tool for healthcare professionals in the screening and diagnosis of Mpox.

title_zh: 用于猴痘疾病检测的 CNN-ViT 和 SE-CNN 与 grad-CAM 的混合架构
source_body_en: Abstract In the aftermath of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the monkeypox virus (MPV) emerged as a significant global health concern, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare it a public health emergency. Accurate detection of monkeypox (Mpox) is challenging due to its similarity to other pox viruses such as measles and chickenpox. Conventional diagnostic methods often struggle to distinguish between these diseases, necessitating the development of more advanced diagnostic tools. This paper presents a novel approach to detect Mpox using two efficient deep learning (DL) models: the first one is a hybrid architecture of a Convolutional Neural Network—Vision Transformer (CNN–ViT), and the second model is a Squeeze-and-Excitation Convolutional Neural Network (SE-CNN). These models are employed for the classification of medical images into two categories: Monkeypox and Others. The proposed models are applied to a dataset of 1140 images, and utilize fine-tuning for the models’ hyperparameters. Data augmentation techniques are implemented for training images to maximize the models’ performance. Additionally, a gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization technique is applied to explain the decision of the models and aid doctors in clinical decision-making. Experimentally, the accuracy, error matrix, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, Recall, F1-score, and Precision are used to measure the performance of the proposed models. The CNN–ViT and SE-CNN achieve a testing accuracy of 97.80% and 96.05%, respectively, while the micro-average area under the ROC curve is 97% for CNN–ViT and 99% for SE-CNN. The weighted F1-score, Precision, and Recall for CNN–ViT are all 97.26%, 97.33%, and 97.27%, respectively, while for SE-CNN are 96.04%, 96.13%, and 96.05%, respectively. The proposed models provide a rapid and accurate method to differentiate Mpox from other cases, offering a valuable tool for healthcare professionals in the screening and diagnosis of Mpox.

title: Serological and molecular evidence of an endemic presence of mpox and associated risk factors in semi-rural areas of southern Cameroon
abstract: The mpox epidemic in Africa is maintained by zoonotic spill-over events and sustained human-to-human transmissions. Our objective in this work was to conduct serological and molecular surveys on the circulation of mpox in Southern Cameroon and associated risk factors. To that end, we conducted cross-sectional surveys and a case investigation between May and August 2025. We screened samples for mpox antibodies and DNA and sequenced PCR-positive samples. Overall, we included 1072 persons (523 women and 549 men) with a median age of 30 years. A total of 122/1072 (11.4%) samples were mpox antibody positive. Seroprevalence was higher in samples collected in August than in May 2025. Risk factors significantly associated with positivity to mpox antibodies were age above 66 years, being widowed, having been bitten at least once by a wild animal and having contact with wildlife. Of the five samples from case investigation, only the index case was PCR-positive (H, 52 years old), confirmed as mpox clade Ia by sequencing (group I). In serology, 2 of the 5 samples of the household (index case and his 13-year-old son) were mpox antibody positive. This pilot work suggests endemic circulation of mpox in the studied semi-rural districts of southern Cameroon.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the endemic presence of mpox and its associated risk factors in semi-rural areas of southern Cameroon, addressing the need to understand the virus's circulation and transmission dynamics in these regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey and case investigation were conducted between May and August 2025 in Southern Cameroon, involving 1072 persons (523 women and 549 men) with a median age of 30 years.
analysis.methods: Samples were screened for mpox antibodies and DNA, and PCR-positive samples were sequenced to determine the clade of the virus.
analysis.main_results: Out of 1072 samples, 122 (11.4%) were mpox antibody positive, and in the case investigation, only the index case was PCR-positive, confirmed as mpox clade Ia by sequencing.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that mpox is circulating endemically in the studied semi-rural districts of southern Cameroon, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and intervention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical insights into the endemic nature of mpox in semi-rural areas, which can inform public health strategies for surveillance, prevention, and control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include a relatively small sample size and potential biases in self-reported risk factors, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the endemic presence of mpox and its associated risk factors in semi-rural areas of southern Cameroon. Conducted between May and August 2025, the cross-sectional survey and case investigation included 1072 individuals, with 11.4% testing positive for mpox antibodies. The index case, confirmed as mpox clade Ia by sequencing, was the only PCR-positive sample in the case investigation. The study suggests that mpox is circulating endemically in the region, emphasizing the need for targeted surveillance and intervention. However, the findings are limited by a relatively small sample size and potential biases in self-reported risk factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title_zh: 喀麦隆南部半农村地区 猴痘 流行的血清学和分子证据及相关危险因素
source_body_en: The mpox epidemic in Africa is maintained by zoonotic spill-over events and sustained human-to-human transmissions. Our objective in this work was to conduct serological and molecular surveys on the circulation of mpox in Southern Cameroon and associated risk factors. To that end, we conducted cross-sectional surveys and a case investigation between May and August 2025. We screened samples for mpox antibodies and DNA and sequenced PCR-positive samples. Overall, we included 1072 persons (523 women and 549 men) with a median age of 30 years. A total of 122/1072 (11.4%) samples were mpox antibody positive. Seroprevalence was higher in samples collected in August than in May 2025. Risk factors significantly associated with positivity to mpox antibodies were age above 66 years, being widowed, having been bitten at least once by a wild animal and having contact with wildlife. Of the five samples from case investigation, only the index case was PCR-positive (H, 52 years old), confirmed as mpox clade Ia by sequencing (group I). In serology, 2 of the 5 samples of the household (index case and his 13-year-old son) were mpox antibody positive. This pilot work suggests endemic circulation of mpox in the studied semi-rural districts of southern Cameroon.

title: Management of Genital Involvement in Monkeypox (MPOX), DRC, April–June 2025
abstract: Introduction: Monkeypox (MPOX) currently constitutes a major public health concern in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the disease remains endemic. Although the generalized cutaneous manifestations of MPOX are relatively well documented in the scientific literature, genital involvement remains insufficiently described, despite its significant clinical, nutritional, psychosocial, and community-related implications. This study aims to describe the clinical, nutritional, and psychosocial characteristics of patients affected by MPOX presenting genital lesions in the Sankuru province. Methods and Materials: This is a descriptive cross-sectional case series conducted in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in the Sankuru province, between April and June 2025. Sociodemographic, clinical, nutritional, therapeutic, and psychosocial data were collected from eight patients with confirmed genital involvement of MPOX. Patients were selected through an exhaustive approach among cases admitted to the Monkeypox Treatment Centers (CTM) in Lodja. The collected information was analyzed to describe the clinical presentation of the disease, the probable transmission routes, and the modalities of integrated patient management. Genital lesions exhibited significantly slower healing compared to cutaneous lesions located on other body areas, with a mean healing time of 21 ± 3.2 days versus 13 ± 2.8 days for peripheral lesions (p < 0.05). Secondary bacterial superinfections were observed in 62.5% of patients. Additionally, two patients (25%) presented severe malnutrition (BMI < 16 kg/m2), which was associated with a significantly longer healing duration, averaging 24 ± 2 days compared to 19 ± 3 days in patients with normal nutritional status (p = 0.04). The probable modes of transmission included sexual transmission (37.5%), intrafamilial transmission (25%), community transmission during social gatherings (25%), and direct spousal transmission (12.5%). A holistic management approach combining medical treatment, nutritional support, and psychosocial care resulted in complete recovery in 87.5% of patients, while adherence to preventive measures was observed in 75% of patients during post-hospital follow-up. Conclusion: Genital involvement in MPOX represents a significant clinical manifestation in the Sankuru province, characterized by slower healing and an increased risk of local complications. These findings highlight the necessity of integrated management combining medical care, nutritional support, psychosocial interventions, and community engagement. Integrating these approaches into public health strategies may contribute to improving the clinical prognosis of patients, reducing disease transmission, and promoting the social and familial reintegration of affected individuals.

These findings highlight the necessity of integrated management combining medical care, nutritional support, psychosocial interventions, and community engagement. Integrating these approaches into public health strategies may contribute to improving the clinical prognosis of patients, reducing disease transmission, and promoting the social and familial reintegration of affected individuals.

source_body_en: Introduction: Monkeypox (MPOX) currently constitutes a major public health concern in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the disease remains endemic. Although the generalized cutaneous manifestations of MPOX are relatively well documented in the scientific literature, genital involvement remains insufficiently described, despite its significant clinical, nutritional, psychosocial, and community-related implications. This study aims to describe the clinical, nutritional, and psychosocial characteristics of patients affected by MPOX presenting genital lesions in the Sankuru province. Methods and Materials: This is a descriptive cross-sectional case series conducted in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in the Sankuru province, between April and June 2025. Sociodemographic, clinical, nutritional, therapeutic, and psychosocial data were collected from eight patients with confirmed genital involvement of MPOX. Patients were selected through an exhaustive approach among cases admitted to the Monkeypox Treatment Centers (CTM) in Lodja. The collected information was analyzed to describe the clinical presentation of the disease, the probable transmission routes, and the modalities of integrated patient management. Genital lesions exhibited significantly slower healing compared to cutaneous lesions located on other body areas, with a mean healing time of 21 ± 3.2 days versus 13 ± 2.8 days for peripheral lesions (p < 0.05). Secondary bacterial superinfections were observed in 62.5% of patients. Additionally, two patients (25%) presented severe malnutrition (BMI < 16 kg/m2), which was associated with a significantly longer healing duration, averaging 24 ± 2 days compared to 19 ± 3 days in patients with normal nutritional status (p = 0.04). A holistic management approach combining medical treatment, nutritional support, and psychosocial care resulted in complete recovery in 87.5% of patients, while adherence to preventive measures was observed in 75% of patients during post-hospital follow-up. Conclusion: Genital involvement in MPOX represents a significant clinical manifestation in the Sankuru province, characterized by slower healing and an increased risk of local complications. These findings highlight the necessity of integrated management combining medical care, nutritional support, psychosocial interventions, and community engagement. Integrating these approaches into public health strategies may contribute to improving the clinical prognosis of patients, reducing disease transmission, and promoting the social and familial reintegration of affected individuals.
abstract_zh: 简介:猴痘 (猴痘) 目前是刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 的一个主要公共卫生问题,该疾病仍然流行。尽管 猴痘 的全身皮肤表现在科学文献中有相对详细的记录,但生殖器受累的描述仍然不充分,尽管其具有显着的临床、营养、心理社会和社区相关影响。本研究旨在描述桑库鲁省受 猴痘 影响、出现生殖器病变的患者的临床、营养和社会心理特征。方法和材料:这是 2025 年 4 月至 6 月在刚果民主共和国桑库鲁省进行的描述性横断面病例系列。从 8 名确诊为 猴痘 生殖器受累的患者收集了社会人口学、临床、营养、治疗和社会心理数据。患者是通过详尽的方法从洛贾猴痘 治疗 中心 (CTM) 收治的病例中选择的。对收集到的信息进行分析,以描述疾病的临床表现、可能的 传播 途径以及综合患者管理的方式。与身体其他部位的皮肤病变相比,生殖器病变的愈合速度明显较慢,平均愈合时间为 21 ± 3.2 天,而周围病变的平均愈合时间为 13 ± 2.8 天 (p < 0.05)。62.5% 的患者出现继发细菌重复感染。此外,两名患者 (25%) 出现严重营养不良 (BMI < 16 kg/m2),这与明显更长的愈合时间相关,平均为 24 ± 2 天,而营养状况正常的患者为 19 ± 3 天 (p = 0.04)。传播的可能模式包括性传播(37.5%)、家庭内传播(25%)、社交聚会期间的社区传播(25%)和直系配偶传播(12.5%)。结合医疗 治疗、营养支持和心理社会护理的整体管理方法使 87.5% 的患者完全康复,而在出院后随访期间观察到 75% 的患者坚持预防措施。结论:猴痘 的生殖器受累是桑库鲁省的一种重要临床表现,其特点是愈合较慢且局部并发症的风险增加。这些发现强调了将医疗护理、营养支持、社会心理干预和社区参与结合起来的综合管理的必要性。将这些方法纳入公共卫生策略可能有助于改善患者的临床预后、减少疾病并促进受影响个体重新融入社会和家庭。

title: Hubungan Pengetahuan dengan Sikap Kader Kesehatan Mengenai Penyakit Mpox di Kota Cirebon
abstract: ABSTRACT Mpox (monkey pox) is a zoonotic disease caused by the orthopox virus. Since May 2022, Mpox cases have increased sharply in various countries including Indonesia. Good knowledge is expected to form a positive attitude in facing the threat of this disease. To determine the relationship between knowledge and attitude of health cadres regarding Mpox disease in Cirebon City. This study used a cross-sectional design with an observational analytic approach. Data collection was conducted in May-June 2025 at 5 health centers in Cirebon City. Respondents consisted of 100 health cadres selected through cluster random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with the Spearman test. The results showed that 53% of cadres had low knowledge, 30% moderate knowledge, and 17% high knowledge. A total of 69% of respondents had a negative attitude towards Mpox prevention, while 31% had a positive attitude. title_zh: Hubungan Pengetahuauan dengan Sikap Kader Kesehatan Mengenai Penyakit 猴痘 井里汶哥打
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Mpox (monkey pox) is a zoonotic disease caused by the orthopox virus. Since May 2022, Mpox cases have increased sharply in various countries including Indonesia. Good knowledge is expected to form a positive attitude in facing the threat of this disease. To determine the relationship between knowledge and attitude of health cadres regarding Mpox disease in Cirebon City. This study used a cross-sectional design with an observational analytic approach. Data collection was conducted in May-June 2025 at 5 health centers in Cirebon City. Respondents consisted of 100 health cadres selected through cluster random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with the Spearman test. The results showed that 53% of cadres had low knowledge, 30% moderate knowledge, and 17% high knowledge. A total of 69% of respondents had a negative attitude towards Mpox prevention, while 31% had a positive attitude. There was a significant and strong relationship between knowledge and attitude of health cadres (p0.001; rho=0.773). Most health cadres in Cirebon City have low knowledge and negative attitudes towards Mpox prevention. There is a strong and significant relationship between knowledge level and attitude. Capacity building of cadres through training and health education is needed to support Mpox prevention efforts. Keywords: Mpox, Knowledge, Attitude, Health Cadres, Cirebon. ABSTRAK Mpox (cacar monyet) adalah penyakit zoonosis yang disebabkan oleh virus orthopox. Sejak Mei 2022, kasus Mpox meningkat tajam di berbagai negara termasuk Indonesia. Pengetahuan yang baik diharapkan dapat membentuk sikap positif dalam menghadapi ancaman penyakit ini. Mengetahui hubungan antara pengetahuan dengan sikap kader kesehatan mengenai penyakit Mpox di Kota Cirebon. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain cross-sectional dengan pendekatan analitik observasional. Pengambilan data dilakukan pada Mei-Juni 2025 di 5 Puskesmas di Kota Cirebon. Responden terdiri dari 100 kader kesehatan yang dipilih melalui cluster random sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner terstruktur dan dianalisis dengan uji Spearman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan 53% kader memiliki pengetahuan rendah, 30% pengetahuan sedang, dan 17% pengetahuan tinggi. Sebanyak 69% responden memiliki sikap negatif terhadap pencegahan Mpox, sementara 31% memiliki sikap positif. Terdapat hubungan yang signifikan dan kuat antara pengetahuan dengan sikap kader kesehatan (p0,001; rho=0,773). Sebagian besar kader kesehatan di Kota Cirebon memiliki pengetahuan yang rendah dan sikap negatif terhadap pencegahan Mpox. Terdapat hubungan yang kuat dan signifikan antara tingkat pengetahuan dengan sikap. Peningkatan kapasitas kader melalui pelatihan dan edukasi kesehatan sangat diperlukan untuk mendukung upaya pencegahan Mpox. Kata Kunci: Mpox, Pengetahuan, Sikap, Kader Kesehatan, Cirebon.

title: HECA-YOLOv11: A High-Accuracy Hybrid Attention Network for Real-Time Monkeypox Skin Lesion Detection with Interpretability
abstract: Introduction: The global outbreak risk of monkeypox necessitates efficient diagnostic tools. Current methods are slow and struggle to differentiate similar skin lesions, while deep learning models lack both accuracy and interpretability for multi-class classification. This study aims to develop a high-performance, real-time screening tool for early detection of monkeypox and similar conditions. Methods: This study proposes an enhanced architecture that incorporates the Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11 to improve feature selection. HECA performs Global Average Pooling (GAP) and Max Average Pooling (MAP) on input feature maps. Using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements, the research establishes and augments a four-class dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images. Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) generates heatmaps for lesion localization visualization, while a PyQt5-based interactive diagnostic interface streamlines clinical workflows. Results: Experimental results demonstrate the proposed model’s superior performance compared to existing approaches (EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, and YOLOv11s) on the test set, with enhanced detection speed, accuracy (98.9%), precision (99%), recall (99.3%), and F1-score (99.1%). HECA-YOLOv11 outperforms SE-YOLOv11 and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all evaluation metrics. Heatmap analysis confirms the model’s focus on lesion regions, aligning with medical reasoning. Discussion: The integrated attention mechanism and interpretability techniques effectively address key limitations in automated skin lesion detection. The high performance and low latency signify a major advancement towards reliable clinical decision support, with important implications for early outbreak containment. Conclusion: The HECA-YOLOv11 framework provides a highly accurate and efficient tool for early monkeypox screening. Its standardized interface holds significant potential to accelerate public health responses and improve global control of emerging infectious diseases.
journal: Recent Advances in Computer Science and Communications

abstract_zh: 简介:全球 暴发 猴痘风险需要高效的诊断工具。目前的方法速度缓慢,并且难以区分相似的皮肤病变,而深度学习模型缺乏多类分类的准确性和可解释性。本研究旨在开发一种高性能、实时筛查工具,用于早期检测猴痘和类似病症。方法:本研究提出了一种增强的架构,将高效通道注意力(HECA)机制纳入 YOLOv11 中,以改进特征选择。HECA 对输入特征图执行全局平均池化 (GAP) 和最大平均池化 (MAP)。该研究利用空间变换和像素域增强,建立并增强了包含猴痘、麻疹、水痘和正常皮肤图像的四类数据集。梯度加权类激活映射 (Grad-CAM) 生成用于病变定位可视化的热图,而基于 PyQt5 的交互式诊断界面则简化了临床工作流程。结果:实验结果表明,与测试集上的现有方法(EfficientNet-v2-l、GoogLeNet、ResNet50、VGG19、MobileNetv2、DenseNet201 和 YOLOv11s)相比,所提出的模型具有优越的性能,具有增强的检测速度、准确度(98.9%)、精确度(99%)、召回率(99.3%)和 F1 分数(99.1%)。在所有评估指标中,HECA-YOLOv11 的性能均优于 SE-YOLOv11 和 ECA-YOLOv11 超过 5.1%。热图分析证实了该模型对病变区域的关注,与医学推理相一致。讨论:集成的注意力机制和可解释性技术有效地解决了自动皮肤病变检测的关键限制。高性能和低延迟标志着可靠临床决策支持的重大进步,对早期 暴发 遏制具有重要意义。结论:HECA-YOLOv11框架为早期猴痘筛查提供了高度准确和高效的工具。其标准化界面在加速公共卫生应对和改善新发传染病的全球控制方面具有巨大潜力。

title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap
abstract: Background: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs). Despite the potential of a One Health approach, current implementations remain fragmented. This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies. Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.
journal: Journal of Clinical Virology and Translational Research

title: Antibodies to distinct epitopes on MPXV enveloped virion provide additive and complete protection.
abstract: The continuing evolution of monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades capable of sustained human-to-human transmission poses an escalating global health risk, yet no effective therapy exists for poxvirus infection. Here, we investigate a panel of human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), derived from an antibody library, which targets A35 and B6 antigens located on the extracellular enveloped virion (EV). Four high-affinity mAbs target the central groove of the A35 dimer, whereas one targets a previously unidentified epitope on the A35 protruding loop. Three other mAbs recognize distinct, previously unmapped epitopes on the multidomain B6 antigen. Those epitopes are conserved across most orthopoxviruses. A combination of an anti-A35 and an anti-B6 antibody provides additive and complete protection from both morbidity and mortality in a lethal VACV mouse model, challenging the previous assumption that targeting both the EV and mature virion (MV) forms is required for full protection. These studies uncover critical information for next-generation therapeutics and vaccines against emerging MPXV as well as other Orthopoxvirus threats.

title: Afanc: taxonomic deconvolution and probabilistic lineage assignment for pathogen genomic surveillance
abstract: Abstract Background: Reliable pathogen genomic surveillance requires both broad tax- onomic sensitivity and high-resolution lineage or clade assignment, yet existing tools usually address only one of these tasks. We developed Afanc as an extensible framework that connects database construction, taxonomic deconvolution and probabilistic lineage assignment from pathogen sequencing data. Afanc source code is available at https://github.com/ArthurVM/Afanc. Results: Afanc integrates automated reference database construction, reference- quality and representativeness filtering, Kraken 2 report deconvolution, com- petitive mapping, variant calling and Bayesian SNP-based classification. We evaluated Afanc across Mycobacteriaceae species and subspecies assignment, mixed Mycobacteriaceae datasets, Mycobacterium tuberculosis lineage classifi- cation, Plasmodium falciparum geolineage prediction and Mpox lineage clas- sification. Afanc resolved Mycobacteriaceae taxa across all simulated coverage cohorts, including 1% genome breadth, and recovered all expected taxa from mixed datasets. tuberculosis, Afanc assigned 955/958 samples at har- monised resolution with no wrong-branch calls. falciparum, Afanc assigned 18,830/20,712 samples to regional lineages, outperforming Malaria-Profiler by 15.8 percentage points. For Mpox, Afanc produced no wrong-branch assignments and achieved 99.4% metadata-resolution-harmonised classification. Conclusions: Afanc provides a reusable framework for moving from noisy broad taxonomic evidence to interpretable lineage-level inference across diverse pathogen systems. By linking database curation, taxonomic deconvolution and probabilistic marker-based classification, Afanc supports pathogen genomic surveillance workflows in which mixed taxonomic signal, incomplete evidence and lineage ambiguity must be handled explicitly before downstream epidemiological or evolutionary interpretation.

abstract_zh: 摘要背景:可靠的病原体 基因组监测 需要广泛的分类敏感性和高分辨率的谱系或进化枝分配,但现有的工具通常只能解决其中一项任务。我们开发了 Afanc 作为一个可扩展框架,连接数据库构建、分类反卷积和病原体测序数据的概率谱系分配。Afanc 源代码可在 https://github.com/ArthurVM/Afanc 获取。结果:Afanc 集成了自动参考数据库构建、参考质量和代表性过滤、Kraken 2 报告反卷积、竞争性映射、变异调用和基于贝叶斯 SNP 的分类。我们评估了分枝杆菌科物种和亚种分配、混合分枝杆菌科数据集、结核分枝杆菌谱系分类、恶性疟原虫地理谱系预测和 猴痘 谱系分类的 Afanc。Afanc 解析了所有模拟覆盖范围 队列研究(包括 1% 基因组 宽度)的分枝杆菌科分类群,并从混合数据集中恢复了所有预期分类群。结核病,Afanc 以统一的分辨率分配了 955/958 个样本,没有错误的分支调用。在恶性疟原虫中,Afanc 将 18,830/20,712 个样本分配给区域谱系,比 Malaria-Profiler 好 15.8 个百分点。对于 猴痘,Afanc 没有产生错误的分支分配,并实现了 99.4% 的元数据分辨率协调分类。结论:Afanc 提供了一个可重用的框架,用于从嘈杂的广泛分类学证据转向跨不同病原体系统的可解释的谱系水平推断。通过链接数据库管理、分类反卷积和基于概率标记的分类,Afanc 支持病原体 基因组监测 工作流程,其中必须在下游流行病学或进化解释之前明确处理混合分类信号、不完整证据和谱系模糊性。

title: Bioinformatics-driven genomic surveillance and evolutionary tracking of emerging viral pathogens
abstract: Emerging viral pathogens pose a persistent threat to global health, making genomic surveillance and evolutionary tracking essential public health tools. This review evaluates bioinformatics tools, pipelines, and analytical approaches for genomic surveillance, pathogen tracking, and real-time evolutionary biology, assessing the strengths, limitations, and pathogen-specific applicability of each. Using a cross-pathogen, comparative framework, we examine five case studies: SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, monkeypox virus (MPXV), avian influenza virus, and honeybee viruses, each requiring a tailored combination of whole-genome sequencing, multiple-sequence alignment, phylogenetic tree building, and molecular clock reconstruction to reconstruct transmission chains and evolutionary dynamics. Key tools discussed include Nextstrain, GISAID, BEAST, IQ-TREE, MEGA, and Pangolin. These approaches have driven tangible public health outcomes, from mRNA vaccine development for SARS-CoV-2 to universal vaccine design efforts for avian influenza, but their impact remains constrained by uneven access to sequencing infrastructure, expertise, and computational resources. Across all five case studies, no single pipeline performs best universally: tool and platform choice must instead be matched to each pathogen’s biology and the surveillance infrastructure available in a given setting. Strengthening this capacity globally, particularly in under-resourced regions, is critical to ensuring emerging pathogens are detected and characterized in time for an effective public health response.

title_zh: 生物信息学驱动的 基因组监测 和新兴病毒病原体的进化追踪
source_body_en: Emerging viral pathogens pose a persistent threat to global health, making genomic surveillance and evolutionary tracking essential public health tools. This review evaluates bioinformatics tools, pipelines, and analytical approaches for genomic surveillance, pathogen tracking, and real-time evolutionary biology, assessing the strengths, limitations, and pathogen-specific applicability of each. Using a cross-pathogen, comparative framework, we examine five case studies: SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, monkeypox virus (MPXV), avian influenza virus, and honeybee viruses, each requiring a tailored combination of whole-genome sequencing, multiple-sequence alignment, phylogenetic tree building, and molecular clock reconstruction to reconstruct transmission chains and evolutionary dynamics. Key tools discussed include Nextstrain, GISAID, BEAST, IQ-TREE, MEGA, and Pangolin. These approaches have driven tangible public health outcomes, from mRNA vaccine development for SARS-CoV-2 to universal vaccine design efforts for avian influenza, but their impact remains constrained by uneven access to sequencing infrastructure, expertise, and computational resources. Across all five case studies, no single pipeline performs best universally: tool and platform choice must instead be matched to each pathogen’s biology and the surveillance infrastructure available in a given setting. Strengthening this capacity globally, particularly in under-resourced regions, is critical to ensuring emerging pathogens are detected and characterized in time for an effective public health response.

title: Spatially Encoded Photonic Microsphere Lens Arrays with Deterministic Hotspaces Enabling Optofluidic Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Chip for Dynamic Monitoring of Multiple Biomarkers.
abstract: Real-time, quantitative dynamic monitoring of multiple biomarkers is urgently needed in clinical practice; however, conventional technologies are limited by cumbersome workflows and time-consuming operational procedures. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) offers high sensitivity and molecular fingerprinting capability, but its application in dynamic monitoring is restricted by signal instability caused by signal irreproducibility arising from stochastic hotspot analyte spatial mismatches, and an exclusive reliance on endpoint measurements that precludes kinetic information extraction. Hence, we present an optofluidic SERS chip integrating spatially encoded photonic microsphere lens arrays (SE-PMLAs) with deterministic hotspaces to overcome these limitations. Through precise integration of gold nanoparticles onto microsphere lens surfaces, each functional unit achieves cascaded photonic-plasmonic coupling among photonic nanojets, whispering-gallery modes, and localized surface plasmon resonance, with near-field feedback reinforcement that transforms random hotspots into engineered, uniform hotspaces, delivering an average enhancement factor of 2.8 × 1010 and signal uniformity with a relative standard deviation below 5%. Using spatially encoded sensing, we demonstrate single-sample, synchronous high-throughput detection of influenza A/B viruses, adenovirus, and monkeypox virus, achieving limits of detection of 0.53 pg/mL, 128.85 copies/mL, 199.56 copies/mL, and 2.7 pg/mL, respectively. Crucially, the chip's ultrastable signal output enables a kinetic quantification model based on the initial binding rate, revealed a linear correlation between analyte concentration and its initial binding rate (i.e., slope). This approach achieves rapid, high-precision dynamic monitoring within 60 to 120s while expanding the linear detection range by two orders of magnitude. Ultimately, this chip delivers a robust, minute-level point-of-care solution for real-time pathogen screening and critical disease diagnostics.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an optofluidic surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) chip that integrates spatially encoded photonic microsphere lens arrays (SE-PMLAs) with deterministic hotspaces to enable real-time, quantitative dynamic monitoring of multiple biomarkers. The chip uses gold nanoparticles to achieve cascaded photonic-plasmonic coupling, transforming random hotspots into engineered, uniform hotspaces. It demonstrates high-throughput detection of influenza A/B viruses, adenovirus, and monkeypox virus with specific limits of detection. The ultrastable signal output allows for kinetic quantification based on initial binding rates, revealing a linear correlation between analyte concentration and binding rate. The chip offers rapid, high-precision monitoring within 60 to 120 seconds and expands the linear detection range by two orders of magnitude. The study does not report limitations or evidence strength, but it presents a novel platform for dynamic pathogen monitoring with potential applications in point-of-care diagnostics and disease surveillance.

title_zh: 具有确定性热空间的空间编码光子微球透镜阵列使光流控表面增强拉曼散射芯片能够动态监测多个生物标记物。
source_body_en: Real-time, quantitative dynamic monitoring of multiple biomarkers is urgently needed in clinical practice; however, conventional technologies are limited by cumbersome workflows and time-consuming operational procedures. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) offers high sensitivity and molecular fingerprinting capability, but its application in dynamic monitoring is restricted by signal instability caused by signal irreproducibility arising from stochastic hotspot analyte spatial mismatches, and an exclusive reliance on endpoint measurements that precludes kinetic information extraction. Hence, we present an optofluidic SERS chip integrating spatially encoded photonic microsphere lens arrays (SE-PMLAs) with deterministic hotspaces to overcome these limitations. Through precise integration of gold nanoparticles onto microsphere lens surfaces, each functional unit achieves cascaded photonic-plasmonic coupling among photonic nanojets, whispering-gallery modes, and localized surface plasmon resonance, with near-field feedback reinforcement that transforms random hotspots into engineered, uniform hotspaces, delivering an average enhancement factor of 2.8 × 1010 and signal uniformity with a relative standard deviation below 5%. Using spatially encoded sensing, we demonstrate single-sample, synchronous high-throughput detection of influenza A/B viruses, adenovirus, and monkeypox virus, achieving limits of detection of 0.53 pg/mL, 128.85 copies/mL, 199.56 copies/mL, and 2.7 pg/mL, respectively. Crucially, the chip's ultrastable signal output enables a kinetic quantification model based on the initial binding rate, revealed a linear correlation between analyte concentration and its initial binding rate (i.e., slope). This approach achieves rapid, high-precision dynamic monitoring within 60 to 120s while expanding the linear detection range by two orders of magnitude. Ultimately, this chip delivers a robust, minute-level point-of-care solution for real-time pathogen screening and critical disease diagnostics.
abstract_zh: 临床迫切需要对多种生物标志物进行实时、定量动态监测;然而,传统技术受到繁琐的工作流程和耗时的操作程序的限制。表面增强拉曼散射 (SERS) 具有高灵敏度和分子指纹识别能力,但其在动态监测中的应用受到信号不稳定的限制,信号不稳定是由于随机热点分析物空间不匹配引起的信号不可再现性,以及对端点测量的完全依赖,从而妨碍了动力学信息提取。因此,我们提出了一种光流控 SERS 芯片,将空间编码光子微球透镜阵列 (SE-PMLA) 与确定性热空间集成,以克服这些限制。通过将金纳米粒子精确集成到微球透镜表面,每个功能单元实现了光子纳米喷射、回音壁模式和局域表面等离子体共振之间的级联光子等离子体耦合,并通过近场反馈增强将随机热点转变为工程化的均匀热空间,提供2.8×1010的平均增强因子和相对标准偏差低于5%的信号均匀性。利用空间编码传感,我们展示了对甲型/乙型流感病毒、腺病毒和猴痘病毒的单样本同步高通量检测,检测限分别达到 0.53 pg/mL、128.85 拷贝/mL、199.56 拷贝/mL 和 2.7 pg/mL。至关重要的是,该芯片的超稳定信号输出支持基于初始结合率的动力学定量模型,揭示了分析物浓度与其初始结合率(即斜率)之间的线性相关性。该方法实现了60至120秒内的快速、高精度动态监测,同时将线性检测范围扩大了两个数量级。最终,该芯片为实时病原体筛查和危重疾病诊断提供了强大的分钟级护理解决方案。

title: สรปการตรวจสอบขาวการระบาดของโรค/ภยสขภาพในรอบสปดาหท 40 ป พ.ศ. 2569
abstract: กรมควบคุมโรค ได้รับรายงานเหตุการณ์ โรค และภัยสุขภาพที่สําคัญ ผ่านโปรแกรมการตรวจสอบข่าวการระบาด กรมควบคุมโรค จากเครือข่ายงานสาธารณสุขทั่วประเทศ ดังนี้ สถานการณ์ในประเทศ 1. อาการผิดปกติเป็นกลุ่มก้อนภายหลังบริโภคผลิตภัณฑ์อาหารเสริม จํานวน 104 ราย อําเภอนาน้อย จังหวัดน่าน 2. โรคฝีดาษวานร (Mpox) เป็นกลุ่มก้อน จํานวน 3 ราย เสียชีวิต 1 ราย จังหวัดอุดรธานี 3. การประเมินความเสี่ยงโรคฝีดาษวานร (Mpox Clade Ib) ในจังหวัดอุดรธานี สถานการณ์ต่างประเทศ กัมพูชายืนยันผู้ป่วยติดเชื้อไข้หวัดนก H5N1 รายที่ 6 ในปี 2569

analysis.research_question_and_background: The supplied evidence does not report a specific research question or knowledge gap; it presents a routine weekly epidemiological surveillance summary from the Thai Department of Disease Control.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a weekly epidemiological surveillance report (week 40, Buddhist year 2569) from the Department of Disease Control, Thailand, compiling nationally reported disease and health events through the national public health network.
analysis.methods: The report uses the Department of Disease Control's epidemic surveillance program to collect and verify reports of important diseases and health events from the nationwide public health network; a risk assessment for Mpox Clade Ib in Udon Thani is mentioned without methodological detail.
analysis.main_results: Four key events are reported: (1) a cluster of 104 cases with abnormal symptoms after consuming food supplements in Na Noi district, Nan province; (2) an Mpox (monkeypox) cluster of 3 cases with 1 death in Udon Thani province; (3) a risk assessment for Mpox Clade Ib in Udon Thani; and (4) Cambodia's confirmation of its 6th human H5N1 avian influenza case in 2026.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The supplied evidence does not report author interpretation or stated novelty beyond the raw surveillance counts and the mention of a Clade Ib risk assessment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide actionable surveillance data on an Mpox Clade Ib cluster with a fatal outcome in Udon Thani, a large food-supplement-associated illness cluster in Nan, and regional H5N1 activity, informing immediate public health response and risk assessment priorities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Evidence is limited to an abstract-only surveillance summary with no methodological detail, denominator data, case definitions, or statistical analysis; the small case numbers (3 Mpox cases, 1 death) and lack of laboratory or epidemiological linkage data constrain confidence, warranting a low evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: The Thai Department of Disease Control's week 40 (2026) epidemiological surveillance report summarizes four national and international health events. Domestically, a cluster of 104 abnormal-symptom cases followed food supplement consumption in Na Noi district, Nan province. In Udon Thani province, an Mpox (monkeypox) cluster comprised 3 cases with 1 death, prompting a specific risk assessment for Mpox Clade Ib. Internationally, Cambodia confirmed its sixth human H5N1 avian influenza case of 2026. The abstract provides case counts and locations but no methodological detail, denominator data, laboratory confirmation methods, or epidemiological linkages. The Mpox Clade Ib cluster with a fatal outcome signals a need for enhanced surveillance and outbreak investigation, while the food-supplement cluster and regional H5N1 case highlight ongoing multi-hazard monitoring. Evidence strength is low due to the abstract-only format, absence of methods, and very small case numbers.

full_text: Abstract This study aimed to develop the Mpox Knowledge Test (M-KT) and the Mpox Preventive Behavior Scale (M-PBS) for the Turkish population and to examine their psychometric properties. For the M-KT, item difficulty, item discrimination, and internal consistency were evaluated, whereas the validity and reliability of the M-PBS were assessed. This methodological study included 449 participants. For the M-KT, content validity, item difficulty, item discrimination, and internal consistency (KR-20) were examined. For the M-PBS, the dataset was randomly divided into two subsamples. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was performed using the first subsample, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with the second. Internal consistency, as well as convergent and discriminant validity, was also evaluated. The M-KT showed satisfactory item characteristics and high internal consistency (KR-20 = 0.915). Similarly, the M-PBS demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Content validity of the M-PBS was adequate (S-CVI/Ave = 0.91). The EFA supported a 13-item, three-factor structure (KMO = 0.919; Bartlett’s test, χ2 = 2047.040, p < 0.001), which explained 62.581% of the total variance. The CFA results indicated an acceptable model fit (RMSEA = 0.076, CFI = 0.952, IFI = 0.952, χ2/df = 2.293). Additional findings provided support for the convergent and discriminant validity of the M-PBS. The M-KT and M-PBS demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and showed evidence of validity and reliability. These instruments may therefore be useful for assessing mpox-related knowledge and preventive behaviors among the Turkish population. Similar content being viewed by others Funding No funding. full_text_excerpt: Abstract This study aimed to develop the Mpox Knowledge Test (M-KT) and the Mpox Preventive Behavior Scale (M-PBS) for the Turkish population and to examine their psychometric properties. This methodological study included 449 participants. The CFA results indicated an acceptable model fit (RMSEA = 0.076, CFI = 0.952, IFI = 0.952, χ2/df = 2.293). Additional findings provided support for the convergent and discriminant validity of the M-PBS. For the M-KT, item difficulty, item discrimination, and internal consistency were evaluated, whereas the validity and reliability of the M-PBS were assessed. For the M-KT, content validity, item difficulty, item discrimination, and internal consistency (KR-20) were examined. For the M-PBS, the dataset was randomly divided into two subsamples. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was performed using the first subsample, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with the second. Internal consistency, as well as convergent and discriminant validity, was also evaluated. The M-KT showed satisfactory item characteristics and high internal consistency (KR-20 = 0.915). Similarly, the M-PBS demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Content validity of the M-PBS was adequate (S-CVI/Ave = 0.91). The EFA supported a 13-item, three-factor structure (KMO = 0.919; Bartlett’s test, χ2 = 2047.040, p < 0.001), which explained 62.581% of the total variance. The M-KT and M-PBS demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and showed evidence of validity and reliability. title: Geospatial analysis and predictive modelling of mpox transmission hotspots: a case study of Ogun State, Nigeria
abstract: Mpox is a recurring public health threat in Nigeria and was re-declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024. Nigeria's Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system operates at the Local Government Area (LGA) level, yet published mpox risk models resolve risk only at state level, forcing uniform deployment across heterogeneous LGAs. This study developed and evaluated an LGA-resolution geospatial risk layer for the 20 LGAs of Ogun State and integrated it, as a proof of concept, into a live surveillance platform. State-level records of 40 laboratory-confirmed cases (NCDC, 2022) and 151 suspected cases (Ogun State Ministry of Health, 2022–2024), 191 in total, were spatially disaggregated into 189 pseudo-presence points and modelled with an ensemble of maximum entropy, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting over 100 bootstrap replicates. Discrimination was good under random hold-out (AUC 0.77; Boyce index 0.99) but fell under spatially blocked cross-validation (AUC 0.57), indicating that the layer is suited to coarse triage between tiers rather than within-tier ranking. Seven LGAs were classified high risk along a central corridor anchored on Abeokuta South and the Ijebu–Remo axis, six medium, and seven low. The tiered layer was exported as GeoJSON with tier-specific action packages and integrated into the IDS-Master platform as a proof-of-concept pathway from spatial epidemiology to routine public health surveillance. Because the 189 points were disaggregated from aggregate counts rather than individually geolocated, the tiers should be read as a spatial prior for triage rather than as confirmed case locations.
